texts.preamble: Shaik Fathima vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 9 February, 2022 Bench: P.Naveen Rao, G.Radha Rani Honourable Sri Justice P.Naveen Rao & Honourable Dr. Justice G.Radha Rani Writ Petition NOs.23492, 23499 and 23504 Of 2021 Date: 09.02.2022 Wp No.23492 of 2021: Between: Shaik Jaibhunnisa, w/o. Shaik Abbas, Aged 56 years, occu; Housewife, r/o. H.No.17-2-138, Beerannakunta, Kareemabad, Warangal District. ..... Petitioner and The State of Telangana, rep.by its Prl.Secretary, General Administration (Spl. Law & Order) Department, Secretariat, Hyderabad and others. .....Respondents The Court made the following: Pnr,J & Grr,J Wp Nos.23492 of 2021 & batch 2 Honourable Sri Justice P.Naveen Rao & Honourable Dr. Justice G.Radha Rani Writ Petition NOs.23492, 23499 and 23504 Of 2021 Common Order:
texts.facts: 3. The detaining authority alleges that the detenues were involved in four crimes, i.e., Crime No.103 of 2021 under Section 395 of IPC, Crime No.104 of 2021 under Section 394 of IPC of Inthezargunj Police Station, Crime No.113 of 2021 under Section 394 of IPC and Crime No.114 of 2021 under Section 394 of IPC of Hasanparthy Police Station. The detenues were arrested on PNR,J & GRR,J WP Nos.23492 of 2021 & batch 20.04.2021. According to the learned counsel for detenues, they have moved bail applications in two crimes, i.e., Crime Nos.113 and 114 of 2021 of Hasanparthy Police Station, but in the meantime they were detained. Because of the preventive detention orders, they were not granted bail in those two bail applications.
texts.arguments: 4. By placing reliance on earlier decision rendered by this Court, following the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, learned counsel for the detenues contends that order of detentions are ex facie illegal, the crimes alleged against the detenues do not warrant resorting to extraordinary measure of preventively detaining them as the offences alleged are under IPC and are triable in accordance with Criminal Procedure Code. He further submits that the detenues are in custody since 20.04.2021 and on account of the orders of detention, their life and liberty is affected for more than nine months and no justification is made, even otherwise, to continue the detention any further. He would further submit that in any case even if detention order is [LEAKAGE_MASK], they cannot be released unless applications to grant bail are moved and competent Court grants them bail. 5. Learned Government Pleader submits that by indulging in crimes registered against them, the detenues are creating panic situation and fear in general public. The Police apprehend that if the detenues are released, they would continue to indulge in committing such crimes and would seriously jeopardize public order. Taking note of the view expressed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Banka Sneha Sheela Vs. The State of Telangana1, this Court held that crimes registered against the detenu would not lead to harm, danger or alarm or feeling of insecurity among the general public, necessitating resorting to such extraordinary measure.
